title: Governed eval signal handoff: Console alerting & dedupe for config/model changes
creator: Omar Velez
description: Build a governed handoff from the evals change detector into Console notification channels (Slack, PagerDuty) that surfaces config and model-change regressions with noise-resistant deduplication and contextual enrichment. This ticket scopes the product/UX, alert routing policies, and acceptance criteria for engineering to implement the Console side integration and runbook wiring.
acceptance_criteria: When a change detector marks a regression tied to a model or config change, Console creates at most one active incident thread per unique regression fingerprint within a 24-hour window.
Alerts include: model version, config diff summary, failing metric names and delta, sample failing inputs and expected/actual snippets, provenance link to the eval run and changelist.
Console UI surfaces a compact rollout-safe card (canary vs prod) that links to eval timelines and the rerun action.
Slack notifications are concise with a direct link to the Console incident thread and a single ‘acknowledge’ action that updates the Console state.
PagerDuty incidents are created only for regressions above the configured severity threshold and respect customer routing rules; duplicates within noise window are suppressed.
Operators can override dedupe keys and escalate via Console; actions are audited and visible in incident history.
End-to-end integration covered by automated e2e tests (mocked eval feed) and an internal runbook describing triage steps and rollback guidance.
updates: 2025-01-16: Kickoff meeting with Eng (Nadia, Priya), SRE (Marcus), and Design (Kei). Aligned on dedupe window default = 24h and fingerprint = (model_id, config_hash, metric, dataset_slice). Action: ENG to validate feasibility of fingerprinting approach.

2025-01-20: ENG-20577 spike results: KV cache of eval identifiers is feasible; memory estimate ~200KB/day per active customer. Trade-off: longer dedupe windows increase memory and cross-customer index complexity. Decision: start with 24h window and expose config knob to Dedicated customers.

2025-01-23: Design review: compact incident card accepted with two CTA buttons (Open eval timeline, Run targeted rerun). Feedback: include sample failing inputs collapsed by default. Design tasked to provide responsive mock for mobile Slack preview.

2025-01-27: Security review intake submitted (security_review_required = false for public telemetry; sensitive artifacts link only for private instances). SRE flagged PD routing for high-severity regressions only; added dependency ENG-21800 for PD escalation policies.

2025-01-30: Wire up Console routes for Slack message actions (acknowledge, mute, open) — prototype implemented in GH PR #1185. Manual QA uncovered race where duplicate Slack messages appear when two eval signals within 10s; ENG added a short-term debounce + idempotency token in PR #4271.

2025-02-02: Product review with Solutions Eng: added 'rollout-safety' label to alerts that reference canary evaluation slices and proposed default severity mapping (canary regressions = P2 by default, prod regressions = P1/P0 depending on magnitude).

2025-02-04: Ready for engineering integration sprint: final acceptance criteria approved, test harness spec added to Confluence, and a staged rollout plan (alpha customers -> beta -> GA). Next: ENG to land dedupe store and console incident API binding; PM to prepare customer communications and runbook training.
